conviction_note: Findings sum to -1.8 (launch-target reset, a back-loaded revenue guide, and a cash/dilution walk on the negative side; a crowded short that has already bounced 22% off the 5 Nov low on the positive side). The scaled number is p_up 46 x abs 11 = -0.88: a mild lean from inference rather than any company number the market has not seen. The negatives are largely visible already (stock -72% from its high, Piper cut YE2026 satellites to 18), and roughly 20% of float is short, so p_up sits only slightly below 50.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus about $44.5M (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-02, via https://finviz.com/news/413750/ast-spacemobiles-plunge-puts-launch-cadence-and-its-150-million-revenue-floor-on-trial) and $46.54M (TIKR, updated 2026-09-26, https://www.tikr.com/blog/ast-spacemobile-promised-150-million-heres-what-has-to-happen-next). The two sources are within 5%. Q4 consensus is $72.62M (TIKR). EPS consensus is -$0.41 against a -$0.48 whisper. The company guide is FY2026 revenue of $150-200M, reiterated 2026-08-10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780312/000119312526342540/asts-ex99_1.htm). H1 was $46.26M, so H2 needs $104-154M. The 'approximately 45 BlueBirds in orbit by early 2027' target sets the bar on the line the stock trades on. It was moved there from end-2026 on 2026-07-15.
positioning_check: Short interest was 64.83M shares with 6.1 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/asts). It was 57.5M and 4.6 days at 2026-08-14 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/asts/short-interest/), and Schaeffer's put it at 21.6% of float in early August (https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/analysis/2026/08/06/heavily-shorted-satellite-stock-gearing-up-for-earnings). That is a crowded and rising short. Baseline 25d skew is +1.98 vol points, a mild put bid, with a put/call OI ratio of 0.64 and the priced lean 'balanced'. Event-implied move is 11.26% (straddle 14.74%). The tape fell from $40.97 (30 Oct) to $30.20 (5 Nov) after the SpaceX/Boost report, then rose to $36.9 at the 2026-11-09 18:10 UTC seal: +22% into the print. The stock is -72% from its 52-week high and -28% over 20 days.

findings.finding: Thirteen BlueBirds were in orbit at the 2026-08-10 update, the last launch was BB11-13 on 2026-08-05, and BB14-16 were 'ready to ship' with no launch date announced in the three months since. The company announces launches about two months ahead. Its 2026-11-06 8-K describes external launch agreements for >100 BlueBirds 'spread over 2027 and 2028'. Reaching 'approximately 45 in orbit by early 2027' would mean about 32 satellites in a few months, so the print most likely re-times that target. Market expectation: Piper Sandler cut its YE2026 forecast from 45 to 18 on 2026-10-13. The company has not yet conceded the 45 target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-15: the last re-timing of the 45-satellite target (end-2026 to early 2027), announced with a $1B convert, was followed by -17.04% (baseline). 2026-04 BB7 wrong orbit: the stock slid (rallies.ai, 2026-04-23).
findings.why_not_priced: Part of this is priced: the stock is -72% off its high and Piper's 18-satellite estimate is public. The company itself still carries '~45 by early 2027' (Trefis 2026-11-03 repeats it as the live target). An explicit reset to a later date or a lower count, with no BB14-16 date, would be a new company statement. If the market had fully priced a reset, the Oct 13 downgrade would have been the bottom. Instead the stock fell another 30% after it, on competition and dilution news rather than on the schedule.
findings.independence: Separate sources. Q2 release (13 in orbit, BB14-16 ready to ship): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780312/000119312526342540/asts-ex99_1.htm. Piper cut to 18 satellites: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/14/ast-spacemobile-falls-8-as-piper-sandler-cuts-target-to-54-on-spacex-competition-rocket-lab-slips/. Advanced Television 2026-08-31, no date or contractor for BB14: https://www.advanced-television.com/2026/08/31/ast-spacemobile-updates-on-progress/

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $150-200M, reiterated three times, needs $104-154M in H2 against H1 of $46.26M (Q1 $14.74M, Q2 $31.52M). Q2 missed consensus by about 8% ($31.5M vs $34.1-35.0M). Consensus has Q3 at $44.5-46.5M and Q4 at $72.6M, above the best-ever quarter of $54.3M (Q4 2025). Revenue is gateway and government milestones, so it is lumpy. Either a Q3 shortfall or a guide trimmed toward or below the $150M floor is the likelier surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-10): revenue missed by about 8% and the guide was held; the stock rose +4.17% (baseline). Q3 2025 (2025-11-10): -1.18%. This name has not sold revenue misses hard. It moves on satellites and financing.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still sits at about $165M for FY, inside the guide, so the Street has not marked to the floor. A guide below $150M would sit outside every published estimate. Mitigant: the revenue line has carried small reactions, which is why this is sized below 1.
findings.independence: Q2 miss and guide from the company release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780312/000119312526342540/asts-ex99_1.htm. Q3 consensus from Earnings Whispers via https://finviz.com/news/413750/ast-spacemobiles-plunge-puts-launch-cadence-and-its-150-million-revenue-floor-on-trial. A TipRanks preview says revenue beat once in eight quarters: https://www.tipranks.com/news/will-ast-spacemobile-stock-asts-rally-or-retreat-after-earnings-today

findings.finding: The Q3 report gives the first cash walk since the July $1.15B convert. Inputs: cash $2.29B plus $428M restricted (Ligado bridge) at June 30, plus the $1.15B convert (about $3.3B usable pro forma); Q3 capex guided $350-425M; H1 FCF -$1.0B. On top of this sits the 2026-11-06 Firefly deal ($400M cash plus 10-14M shares upfront, then $500M over three years). Analysts put cash burn at about $3.1B from July 2026 through 2028 before Firefly. Any ATM use in Q3 under the October 2025 equity distribution agreement, or a new raise plan, lands at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing days were sold hard: 2026-07-15 convert -17.04%, 2026-02-11 registered direct plus convert -15.17%, 2025-10-21 -9.24% (baseline, non-earnings). But the 2026-11-06 Firefly commitment of $1.3B, partly in stock, was bought +1% (Reuters via bdnews24) to +7% (TIKR).
findings.why_not_priced: The Sept 30 balance and any Q3 ATM issuance are not public until the 10-Q and release. The market bought the Firefly news, which suggests it has not netted the $400M cash and 3-5% dilution against the runway. The answer on what the money buys matters here: it funds launch capacity, the binding constraint, and $1.3B of backlog corroborates demand. It does not help 2027 deployments, and no going-concern flag appears. So the finding is a small negative, not a distress call.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 for the Firefly terms (8-K ex99-1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780312/000149315226050513/ex99-1.htm). Separately, a class action alleges overstated capital sufficiency: https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/211375/AST-SpaceMobile-ASTS-Deadline-Approaching-Berger-Montague-Advises-Investors-of-Deadline-in-Securities-Fraud-Lawsuit

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q lists Verizon's $45.0M commercial prepayment as still owed. It is creditable against future service revenue and conditioned on regulatory approvals (FCC commercial SCS authority granted 2026-04-22) and a definitive commercial agreement. Q3 shows whether it was received, which would be evidence a definitive Verizon agreement was signed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a prepayment. The Verizon partnership announcement (2024) was bought sharply (TipRanks: '+50% on new partnership').
findings.why_not_priced: Only one preview flags it (TIKR, 2026-11-07). If it were priced, a received prepayment would already be in consensus cash, and no source carries it. It is small against the cash pile, but a definitive Verizon agreement would partly answer the SpaceX/Boost competition worry. The outcome is unknown, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The TIKR preview names it as one of four things the report must show: https://www.tikr.com/blog/ast-spacemobile-fell-26-in-a-week-the-november-9-report-has-to-answer-the-dilution-question

findings.finding: Positioning: 64.83M shares short at 2026-09-30 with 6.1 days to cover, up from 57.5M and 4.6 days in mid-August (about 21% of float per Schaeffer's). findings.why_not_priced: The skew (+1.98) and put/call OI (0.64) are near-neutral, so options are not pricing a squeeze. The short count was still rising into the last settlement. The 22% bounce into the print shows some covering has started, and that tempers the size.

findings.finding: The Washington Post reported on 2026-11-02 that SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile or use its network (Boost leases capacity from AT&T and T-Mobile), and ASTS fell 11% that day. The call is management's first chance to answer the competitive threat to its carrier-partner model. The answer can cut either way. Unconfirmed by SpaceX or EchoStar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-11-02: -11% on the report (Stocktwits). 2026-10-13: Piper's SpaceX-competition downgrade, -8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline is priced (-11%, then -26% on the week). What is not priced is whether a deal or its confirmation lands inside the window, and how management answers. That is a coin flip leaning slightly negative, because AST has no lever on SpaceX.

baseline_tension: The findings lean negative, which agrees with the mild put skew (+1.98) and the -28% 20-day run-up. A crowded, still-rising short and a +22% bounce off the lows into the print cut against them, so the lean is kept small and p_up sits at 46, not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, about 21% of float, 6.1 days to cover and rising): launch-target finding -2.0 to -1.5, revenue finding -1.0 to -0.7. p_up 45 to 46.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the Firefly money buys launch capacity, the binding constraint, against $1.3B of backlog. No going-concern flag, and the market bought the 2026-11-06 news. Financing finding -1.0 to -0.5, kept negative only for the unknown Q3 ATM and cash walk.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): the Q2 revenue miss was bought +4.17%, so revenue stays small. print_vs_bar eased from -4 to -3 because the two consensus sources disagree by about $2M.

Base rate rebuilt from confirmed earnings dates only (Aug-26 +4.17, May-26 -11.62, Mar-26 +6.63, Nov-25 -1.18; the Jul-26, Feb-26 and Oct-25 rows are financing days). Median about 5.4% against the 11.26% implied, so abs_move went from 12 to 11, kept near the implied move because a guidance-type reset is likely.
Lesson 6: the bar is sourced to two estimate sources within 5% plus a company FY guide, so no cap was needed. Blacklift (11-12) and the class action (11-13) stay in outside_window.
